Essays on daylight

A monthly letter about light, rooms, and the hours we keep.

The morning room faces east, and in March the sun arrives before the kettle boils.

We have measured the same windowsill every equinox for eleven years now.

South-facing glass earns its keep in winter and begs for shade in August.

A room painted white is a room that borrows light from every hour.

Curtains are for privacy; shutters are for deciding what the day means.

Lumen Field Notes — published from Lisbon
